subtitle: The grids, pyramids, loops, curves and diagrams that people use to think clearly — in business, psychology, medicine, schools, science, the army and everyday life.
intro: What are these tools called? There is no single official name. People call them frameworks or models. A grid is a matrix (plural: matrices), and a four-box grid is a 2×2 (say “two-by-two”). Researchers who sort people or things into types call the result a typology.

How many are there? Nobody knows — hundreds, and new ones appear every year. Most collections choose the best 50 to 80. This toolbox holds the ones you are most likely to meet, in six families, grouped by their shape. The shape tells you how the tool thinks: a grid sorts, a pyramid ranks, a loop repeats, a curve shows a pattern, a diagram connects, and a checklist makes sure nothing is forgotten.
Are they only for business? No. Use the buttons below to see the same kind of thinking in psychology, medicine, education, the military and politics. Tools marked lesson have a full lesson.
dash_intro: A manager sorts a whole team into nine boxes. A president divides his day into four. A fighter pilot turns a dogfight into a loop, and a Japanese chemist draws a fish. Every one of these is a thinking tool — a simple shape that turns a messy problem into a few clear questions.

Each lesson tells the true story of one tool: who drew it, what problem they had, and what happened next. Then you use the tool yourself, learn one grammar point the tool needs, and finish by applying it to your own life and work. Start with the map, or pick any card — the lessons can be taken in any order.

families.name: Grids & matrices
families.desc: Take two questions, cross them, and every item falls into a box. The most popular shape of all.

tools.name: The 9-Box Grid
tools.who: HR use from the 1970s–90s, adapted from the GE–McKinsey matrix
tools.what: Sorts employees by performance now and potential for the future.

tools.name: The Eisenhower Matrix
tools.who: Named after Dwight Eisenhower (1954); made famous by Stephen Covey (1989)
tools.what: Sorts tasks by urgent / not urgent and important / not important.

tools.name: The Johari Window
tools.what: Four “panes” of what you and others know about you.

tools.name: The Prisoner's Dilemma
tools.who: Flood & Dresher at RAND, 1950; story by Albert Tucker
tools.what: A payoff grid showing why two sensible people may both refuse to cooperate.

tools.name: The BCG Matrix
tools.what: Stars, cash cows, question marks and dogs: sorts a company's products.

tools.name: The GE–McKinsey Matrix
tools.what: A nine-box grid for deciding which businesses to invest in.

tools.name: The Ansoff Matrix
tools.what: Four ways to grow: old or new products, in old or new markets.

tools.name: The Risk Matrix
tools.what: Likelihood × impact: how worried should we be about each risk?

tools.name: The Stakeholder Grid
tools.what: Power × interest: who to keep close, who to keep informed.

tools.name: The Skill–Will Matrix
tools.what: Ability × motivation: tells a manager whether to guide, push, excite or delegate.

tools.name: The Impact–Effort Matrix
tools.what: Quick wins, big projects, fill-ins and time-wasters.

tools.name: The Parenting Styles Model
tools.what: Warmth × control: authoritative, authoritarian, permissive, neglectful.

tools.name: Berry's Acculturation Model
tools.what: How migrants live between two cultures: integration, assimilation, separation, marginalisation.

tools.name: The Conflict Modes Grid
tools.what: Five ways people handle conflict, from avoiding to collaborating.

tools.name: The Confusion Matrix
tools.what: True and false positives and negatives: how good is a test?

tools.name: The Punnett Square
tools.what: Predicts the genes a child may inherit from two parents.

tools.name: The “Known Unknowns” Grid
tools.what: What we know, what we know we don't know — and what we don't even know we don't know.

tools.name: The Political Compass
tools.what: Places political views on left–right and freedom–authority axes.

families.name: Pyramids & ladders
families.desc: Levels stacked on top of each other: the bottom must be solid before you climb.

tools.name: Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs
tools.who: Abraham Maslow, 1943 (the pyramid drawing came later)
tools.what: Human needs in five levels, from food and safety up to growth.

tools.name: Bloom's Taxonomy
tools.what: Levels of thinking, from remembering up to creating.

tools.name: The Minto Pyramid
tools.what: Put the answer first, then the reasons, then the details.

tools.name: The Food Pyramid
tools.what: What to eat most and least — since replaced by plates in many countries.

tools.name: The Ladder of Inference
tools.what: How we climb from facts to assumptions to beliefs — often too fast.

tools.name: Arnstein's Ladder of Participation
tools.what: Eight rungs of how much real power citizens have.

tools.name: The Hierarchy of Controls
tools.what: Remove the danger first; protective clothing comes last.

tools.name: The Kirkpatrick Model
tools.what: Four levels for judging whether training worked.

families.name: Cycles & loops
families.desc: Steps that come round again. The point is not to finish but to keep turning — faster and better.

tools.name: The OODA Loop
tools.what: Observe, orient, decide, act — faster than your opponent.

tools.name: Plan–Do–Check–Act
tools.what: The improvement cycle behind Japan's quality revolution.

tools.name: Kolb's Learning Cycle
tools.what: Experience, reflect, think, try again.

tools.name: Gibbs' Reflective Cycle
tools.what: Six questions for learning from an experience — loved by nurses and teachers.

tools.name: The Scientific Method
tools.what: Question, hypothesis, test, conclude, repeat.

tools.name: The Design Thinking Cycle
tools.what: Empathise, define, ideate, prototype, test.

tools.name: The Product Life Cycle
tools.what: Introduction, growth, maturity, decline.

tools.name: The Stages of Change
tools.what: How people change habits — from not ready to maintaining.

tools.name: Tuckman's Team Stages
tools.what: Forming, storming, norming, performing, adjourning.

families.name: Curves & rules
families.desc: A line on a chart that shows a pattern — and a rule of thumb that grows out of it.

tools.name: The Pareto Principle
tools.who: Vilfredo Pareto, 1896; named by Joseph Juran, 1940s
tools.what: A few causes produce most of the results.

tools.name: The Diffusion of Innovations
tools.what: How new ideas spread: innovators, early adopters… laggards.

tools.name: The Hype Cycle
tools.what: Excitement, disappointment, then real use — the path of new technology.

tools.name: The Forgetting Curve
tools.what: How fast we forget — and why review works.

tools.name: The Yerkes–Dodson Curve
tools.what: A little pressure helps performance; too much hurts it.

tools.name: The Bell Curve
tools.what: Most results sit in the middle; few sit at the extremes.

tools.name: The Experience Curve
tools.what: Each time total production doubles, costs fall by a steady amount.

tools.name: The S-Curve
tools.what: Slow start, fast growth, then a plateau.

families.name: Diagrams & maps
families.desc: Boxes, branches and arrows that show how things connect — causes, steps, overlaps.

tools.name: The Fishbone Diagram
tools.what: Maps every possible cause of one problem.

tools.name: The Venn Diagram
tools.what: Overlapping circles showing what things share.

tools.name: Ikigai
tools.who: Western diagram (2010s) inspired by a Japanese word
tools.what: Where what you love, what you're good at, what the world needs and what pays overlap.

tools.name: The Mind Map
tools.what: Ideas branching out from one central topic.

tools.name: The Flowchart
tools.what: Boxes and arrows showing each step and decision in a process.

tools.name: The Decision Tree
tools.what: Each branch is a choice or a chance, with its possible results.

tools.name: Porter's Value Chain
tools.what: The chain of activities where a company adds value.

tools.name: The Five Whys
tools.what: Ask “why?” five times to reach the root cause.

tools.name: The Cynefin Framework
tools.what: Is the situation clear, complicated, complex or chaotic? Each needs a different response.

families.name: Checklists & canvases
families.desc: A set of headings that makes sure nothing is forgotten — often remembered as a short word.

tools.name: SWOT Analysis
tools.what: Strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats.

tools.name: PESTLE
tools.what: Political, economic, social, technological, legal, environmental forces.

tools.name: Porter's Five Forces
tools.what: Five pressures that decide how profitable an industry can be.

tools.name: The McKinsey 7-S
tools.what: Seven parts of an organisation that must fit together.

tools.name: The 4 Ps of Marketing
tools.what: Product, price, place, promotion.

tools.name: SMART Goals
tools.what: Specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, time-bound.

tools.name: The Business Model Canvas
tools.what: Nine boxes that describe how any business makes money.

tools.name: Six Thinking Hats
tools.what: Look at a problem six ways: facts, feelings, risks, benefits, ideas, process.

tools.name: AIDA
tools.who: Attributed to Elias St. Elmo Lewis, 1898
tools.what: Attention, interest, desire, action: the path of an advert.

tools.name: The Surgical Safety Checklist
tools.what: A short checklist that cut deaths and complications in operating theatres.

tools.name: ABCDE
tools.what: Airway, breathing, circulation, disability, exposure — check in this order.
